_note: Joke of the Day 🥞. One per day, picked by build date (PT). Keep them clean, original, and never about a specific company.
jokes: Why did the maple tree hire a financial advisor? Its sap was getting tapped out.
My portfolio is like maple syrup: slow, sticky, and mostly Canadian.
What's a lumberjack's favourite investment? Dividend log-ristocrats.
Why don't maple trees panic in a crash? They know the sap always runs again in spring.
Why did the pancake open a TFSA? It wanted its stack to grow tax-free.
What do you call a maple tree that pays you every quarter? A sap-ital gain.
My financial plan has two steps: buy dividend stocks, then buy more syrup with the dividends.
Why was the syrup bottle so calm during the market dip? It was used to being under pressure in March.
I told my pancakes about compound interest. Now they want to be a stack of stacks.
Why do Canadians make great long-term investors? We're used to waiting six months for spring.
What did the waffle say to the dividend? "You fill all my little squares."
Bear markets are just syrup season in reverse: everything drains out of the bucket for a while.
How does a maple tree check its returns? It looks at its sap-shot.
Why did the moose start investing? He heard about bull markets and wanted a herd.
My broker asked about my risk tolerance. I said I put syrup on bacon, so pretty high.
What's the sweetest part of a balance sheet? The retained earnings, after a long boil.
Why did the beaver diversify? It didn't want all its logs in one dam.
I asked the maple tree for a hot stock tip. It said, "Be patient. Good things take 40 litres of sap."
Why are dividend investors good at breakfast? They know the best part is the payout on top.
What do you call a toque that pays monthly? A cash-flow cap.
My savings plan is like a sugar shack: lots of steam, but the good stuff adds up.
Why did the hockey player buy dividend stocks? He liked getting paid between periods.
How do pancakes rebalance? They flip.
Why did the loonie go to the gym? It wanted to be a toonie.
What's a maple tree's favourite chart? A candle-stack with extra syrup.
My spreadsheet is 90% dividend dates and 10% pancake recipes. It's called balance.
Why did the squirrel love index funds? It could own a little of every nut.
What do you get when you reinvest your syrup? A DRIP-ping stack.
Why was the canoe a good investor? It never tried to time the rapids.
Why don't maple trees day trade? They prefer to grow one ring a year.
I tried to explain the yield curve to my pancakes. They just stayed flat.
How does a snowman invest? Cold, calculated, and only in frozen assets.
Why did the syrup refuse to sell in a panic? It's naturally slow to move.
What's a Canadian investor's favourite weather? A steady drizzle of dividends.
Why did the maple leaf join the market? It wanted to turn over a new leaf every quarter.
My retirement plan is simple: be the tree, not the pancake.
What did the ex-dividend date say to the latecomer? "Sorry, eh. The syrup's already been poured."
Why did the pancake stack ask for a raise? It felt a little short.
Why did the goose fly south with a brokerage app? It wanted to check foreign markets.
How many dividend investors does it take to change a light bulb? One, but they'll wait for the ex-date first.
Why is maple syrup like a good stock? Grade A, and it gets better the longer you leave it alone.
What do maple trees do on payday? They throw a little sap-ening.
I put my dividends in a jar labelled "syrup money." It's the fastest-growing jar in the house.
Why did the market go to the sugar shack? It needed a sweet rebound.
What do you call a stock that only goes up in maple season? Sap-preciation.
Why did the toboggan avoid leverage? It already goes downhill fast enough.
My pancakes and my portfolio have one rule: never skimp on the base.
Why did the maple tree get a great credit score? It always paid back in spring.
What's a lumberjack's least favourite market? A choppy one.
How do you know an investor is Canadian? They apologize to the market for buying the dip.
Why did the bucket under the tap feel rich? Every drip was compounding.
What did the bond say to the dividend stock? "Must be nice to get a raise."
Why do maple trees love long weekends? Three days of sap, no closing bell.
My investing style is like a maple farmer's: tap, wait, boil, repeat.
Why did the pancake become a fund manager? It had great flip-ping experience.
What do you call a dividend paid in syrup? A liquid asset.
Why are maple trees bad at gossip? They only spill the sap in spring.
What's the best time to plant a maple tree or buy a dividend stock? Twenty years ago. The second best is breakfast.
Why did the cabin buy a dividend fund? It wanted a little passive income by the woodstove.
What's the difference between a sugar maple and a growth stock? One takes 40 years to tap; the other just feels like it.
